URL: https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/4-detained-north-macedonia-alleged-iran-backed-assassination-138214034
ABC News (AP wire), 17 Nov 2026 11:01 GMT

ShareFollow ABC News on GoogleSKOPJE, North Macedonia -- Authorities in North Macedonia have detained four people for questioning over an alleged Iran-linked assassination plot in neighboring Greece, officials said Tuesday.

Bojan Hristovski, director of North Macedonia's domestic security agency, said Tuesday that the suspects are all Macedonian citizens, adding that a fifth person had also been questioned and a sixth remained wanted by the authorities.

Hristovski named one of the Iranian recruiters as Naji Sharifi Zindashti, who is wanted in the United States for allegedly operating a criminal network that targets Iranian dissidents and activists abroad.

He did not give details of the alleged target in Greece, and Greek authorities did not immediately comment on the announcement.

“This concerns the dismantling of an Iranian proxy network involved in planning a terrorist attack,” Hristovski said.

“The network operating in Macedonia consisted of individuals embedded in criminal organizations within the country,” he said. “Acting on direct instructions from an Iranian national, they undertook preparatory and logistical activities for a terrorist act — an assassination targeting a previously identified individual located in Greece.”

Iran's mission to the United Nations did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
